decisions.reason: The dashboard changes do not alter the explanation content requirement; the separate bullet-format and page-one concision changes from the same message are already represented.
Changing the score dashboard does not alter the independently specified vehicle-group presentation, which already reflects its own clause from the source message.
The front-page score heading and prominence changes do not change which customer fields must remain editable; the assessment-date refinement is already represented separately.
The dashboard refinement does not require an additional change to the broad visual-design state, whose same-message design-direction and refinement updates are already recorded.
The front-page dashboard modification does not alter the final-page confidentiality warning, which is governed by a separate clause in the source message.
The dashboard modification does not change the internal-page header; its page coverage, style, and information were independently modified by another clause already represented at message 42.
The dashboard decision leaves the footer requirement unchanged, and the source message explicitly reports that the existing footer is working well.
The score-dashboard modification does not alter the required RR-01 footer code; that code requirement is already established directly from the separate report-code clause.
The score heading and dashboard layout changes do not alter the RR-01 identifier required in the internal header, which is already represented.
The dashboard modification does not change the RR-01 report-detail identifier; the source message's independent code-consistency instruction is already represented in this candidate.
The front-page score heading, prominence, and immediate visibility changes do not alter the scoring summary table's fields, format, or purpose.
Applying a dashboard refinement does not change the required four report variants or their score/risk-based selection rule.
